summary: Tested the message rival, granting the link premise, against critical witnesses and the multiple-attestation argument for a governing commission. Correction on resume (2026-10-31): the 2026-10-27 draft attributed to Harnack, History of Dogma I, ch. II §3, note 76, an event-level denial that Jesus gave the ekklēsia its judging power, chosen because §2 denies a founded community. Re-read: the note's subject is the designation ἐκκλησία and it says only that 'the words of the Lord, Matt. XVI. 18; XVIII. 17, belong to a later period', without saying later than what and without argument. That attribution was an over-read and is removed: the claim now reads the dating only (STMT-MATT-16-18-18-17-SAYINGS-LATER), and the strengthening is the unattributed STMT-JUDGING-POWER-NOT-GIVEN-BY-JESUS. A wording-only reading is therefore not rejected for the note. New witness: Renan, Life of Jesus (Gutenberg 16581, plain text), ch. XVIII read in full: Jesus 'confided to the Church the right to bind and to unbind ..., to remit sins', note 11 citing Matt. xviii. 17 ff. and John xx. 23, then 'It is possible that many of these words may have been attributed to the master, in order to give a warrant to the collective authority' (STMT-COMMUNITY-ATTRIBUTION-OF-CHURCH-POWERS-POSSIBLE). It is a possibility, about many words; Renan elsewhere in the chapter says Jesus laid the foundation of a church, so he is not a message-only rival. Also found, not pinned: Renan ch. IX, 'At one time he seems even to promise him "the keys"... decisions which should always be ratified in eternity', note 8 citing Matt. xvi. 19 and xviii. 18 (a hedged report, no denial). Strauss, Life of Jesus Critically Examined (Gutenberg 64037), on Matt. xviii. 17: the ekklēsia is either the synagogue or, if the Christian community, 'at least in the form of expression, an anticipation of a subsequent state of things', and 'the writer certainly had in view the new church' when representing Jesus as imparting binding and loosing; on John xx. 22 f. he writes 'comp. Matt. xviii. 18'; not pinned for the PR file limit and because it is disjunctive, and no event denial. Harnack, History of Dogma II (Gutenberg 19613), note 334 and its text: Calixtus's appeal to Matt. XVI. 18 ff. is 'the first instance of the kind recorded in history', which dates a use, not the saying; not pinned. No witness found denies Matthew 16.17-19 as a whole; verse 17 is a beatitude and names no power. Derived, conditional only: the link premise, John 20's independence of Matthew 18 or 16, and the criterion for this family exclude the message rival wherever Jesus holds a mandate and founded the Catholic Church (CATHOLICISM-MESSAGE-RIVAL-EXCLUDED-BY-ATTESTATION; three omission models; joint model). The critical fork in CommissionAttestation: a denial of the powers of Matthew 16.19 (keys, binding and loosing, to any recipient) with the two attestation premises yields only forgiving and retaining (matt16PowersNotGiven_forces_john), and is jointly satisfiable with the report-to-event premise (matt16PowersNotGiven_compatible); a denial of the whole family rejects independence or the criterion (familyNotGiven_rejects_attestation), and is satisfiable with independence and a false criterion (familyNotGiven_with_independence). A rival granting the link premise, mandate and founding must do the latter (rivalWithFounding_rejects_attestation). No historical confidence is proved: independence and the criterion stay unsourced, and Power does not separate the singular Matthew 16.19 from the plural 18.18. The attestation premises do not give STMT-COMMISSION-REPORTS-GO-BACK-TO-JESUS (attestation_not_reports); with Matthew 28 they would give the narrow premise (narrow_from_attestation), not recorded because it replaces a sourced premise with unsourced ones. Galatians read in pinned NT-GAL-2 and NT-GAL-1: 1.18 Paul went up 'historēsai Kēphan' and stayed fifteen days; 2.7-8 the one who worked through Peter for the apostleship of the circumcision worked through Paul for the Gentiles; 2.9 James, Cephas and John, 'hoi dokountes styloi einai', gave the right hand of fellowship; 2.6 the reputed ones added nothing to him; 2.11-14 he opposes Cephas. It reports reputation, names James first and mentions no commission of Jesus; both a commission and the first appearance (1 Corinthians 15.5) would explain it. Non-discriminating, so no statement or claim was kept (the draft's records were dropped; invariant: no claim merely to record activity). Source search for the criterion and John's independence: Gutenberg has no Burkitt, Hort or Expositor's Greek Testament; Sanday, Criticism of the Fourth Gospel (Gutenberg 60553) does not discuss John 20.23; Catholic Encyclopedia 'Primacy' and 'The Pope' give no independence argument; Meier, Dodd and Brown are copyrighted and were not read, so no bibliographic span was created. Remaining blocker: a pinned or read source for the criterion and for John's independence, and a critical source denying 16.19, 18.18 or John 20.23 outright. Frontier: no change (the conclusion reaches no root route).
